findings: Unsupported SAMPLE assertions: course duration/content, identity-check method, attendance, specific log names, system version, interviews, sampling randomness, and data completeness were invented beyond the supplied dataset.

Unapproved numeric thresholds: 80/85 percent, ±25 percent workload, 30 percent leave, 1 percent missing records, ±5pp/10pp decision cutoffs, and n=20 HOLD rule are not supported by official source; they must not be presented as institutional standards.
Confounder status column asserts verification where the source marks real-world status unknown.
Evidence chain invents synthetic original records not present in the registered sample inputs.
Wording/genre issues include use of statistical significance language without a test and a typo in the intervention description.
Need clarify that suggested controls are proposals, not association decisions or verified events.
